questions.title: Lower Cumulative Tail of a Binomial Distribution

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(8, 0.3)$. Find $P(X \le 2)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Upper Tail Probability Using Direct Exact Terms

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(10, 0.65)$. Find $P(X \ge 8)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Strict Inequality: Fewer Than Three Underweight Bags

parts.text: A bag of flour is underweight with probability $0.12$, independently of other bags. Ten bags are selected at random. Let $X$ be the number of underweight bags. Find the probability that fewer than 3 bags are underweight, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Strict Upper Bound: More Than Five Successes

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(7, 0.4)$. Find $P(X > 5)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Inclusive Interval for a Symmetric Binomial Distribution

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(6, 0.5)$. Find $P(2 \le X \le 4)$, giving your answer as an exact decimal or fraction.

questions.title: Using the Upper Complement for 'No More Than'

parts.text: A parcel is delivered on time with probability $0.58$, independently of other parcels. For a batch of 9 parcels, find the probability that no more than 6 are delivered on time, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Lower Cumulative and Upper Tail in Eight Trials

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(8, 0.25)$. Find $P(X \le 1)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find $P(X \ge 3)$.

questions.title: Delivery Delays: Strict Upper Bound and Middle Range

parts.text: A postal service has a $15\%$ delay rate on parcels, independently of other parcels. A customer posts 7 parcels. Let $X$ be the number of delayed parcels. Find the probability that fewer than 2 parcels are delayed, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that between 2 and 4 parcels inclusive are delayed.

questions.title: Middle Interval and Upper Tail in Twelve Trials

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(12, 0.26)$. Find $P(2 \le X \le 4)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find $P(X > 4)$.

In a municipal survey, a resident supports a proposed zoning policy with probability $0.47$, independently of other residents. Nine residents are selected at random. Let $X$ be the number of residents who support the policy. Find the probability that more than 2 but fewer than 8 residents support the policy.
Given that more than 2 but fewer than 8 residents support the policy, find the probability that at least 5 residents support the policy.

questions.title: Call Centre Service Level: Upper Tail and Restricted Range

parts.text: A customer support desk successfully resolves a caller enquiry within 5 minutes with probability $0.70$, independently for each call. Ten calls are monitored at random. Let $X$ be the number of calls resolved within 5 minutes. Find the probability that at least 7 calls are resolved within 5 minutes.
Given that at least 7 calls are resolved within 5 minutes, find the probability that at most 8 calls are resolved within 5 minutes.

questions.title: Nursery Seed Trays: Cumulative Bounds and Compound Binomial Model

parts.text: A batch of treated seeds has an $80\%$ germination rate, independently of other seeds. A nursery tray contains 12 seeds. Let $X$ be the number of germinating seeds in a tray. Find the probability that at least 10 seeds germinate in a randomly chosen tray, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that fewer than 9 seeds germinate in a randomly chosen tray.

A tray is classified as 'premium' if at least 10 seeds germinate. A commercial nursery inspects a random sample of 6 independent trays. Find the probability that at least 4 of the 6 trays are classified as premium.

questions.title: Examination Grading: Cumulative Bounds, Inclusive Intervals, and Conditional Probabilities

parts.text: In a certain mathematics module examination, the pass rate is $65\%$, independently for each candidate. A group of 11 candidates takes the examination. Let $X$ be the number of candidates who pass. Find the probability that at most 6 candidates pass, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that between 6 and 9 candidates inclusive pass the examination.
Given that at most 8 candidates pass, find the probability that at least 6 candidates pass.
